synopsis: Active-learning or Bayesian test selection can efficiently learn decision boundaries, conditional on an assumed surrogate model and acquisition model [f6860]. The glossary distinguishes the methods by objective: active learning aims to learn a boundary, whereas Bayesian optimization aims to find the best or worst setting [f14175]. Both use adaptive selection guided by a surrogate model and an acquisition rule [f14175]. A key limitation is that the surrogate’s uncertainty estimate can itself be wrong, qualifying the claimed efficiency of this approach [f6862, f6860].

relations.note: Defines the selection mechanism and distinguishes boundary learning from best-or-worst-setting optimization.
Identifies unreliable surrogate uncertainty as a limitation of model-dependent efficient selection.
